variables.reason: The ledger defines Ra as the first-order absolute moment (mean absolute deviation) of surface height fluctuations. The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness has the same canonical quantity name (arithmetic mean roughness), lists symbols including Ra and R_a, gives the identical definition (mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean), and specifies si_unit = m and si_dimension = L. This record therefore directly documents that Ra is a dimensional length quantity and supports the L=1 exponent in the candidate vector.

The ledger defines kt as the peak-to-valley height (height difference between maxima and minima). The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height uses symbols including kt, describes the same physical measure (a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences between peaks and valleys), and lists si_unit = m and si_dimension = L. This directly justifies treating kt as a length (L=1) in the candidate vector.

The ledger defines k_rms as the root-mean-square height of surface fluctuations. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height gives the canonical quantity 'root-mean-square roughness height', uses the same symbol k_rms, and states si_unit = m and si_dimension = L. This corroborates that k_rms carries physical length dimension (L=1) as in the candidate vector.

The ledger labels Sk as skewness of roughness height fluctuations (third standardized moment). The KB record pq_height_skewness defines 'surface-height skewness', lists symbols including Sk, explicitly states it is a dimensionless standardized moment (si_dimension = 1) and provides domain context (surface roughness). This confirms the candidate's all-zero (dimensionless) exponents.

The ledger identifies Ku as kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment). The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines 'surface-height kurtosis', uses symbol Ku, and explicitly states it is dimensionless (si_dimension = 1). Thus Ku is correctly represented as dimensionless (all exponents zero) in the candidate vector.

The ledger defines ES as the effective streamwise slope (mean absolute gradient of surface height). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope describes 'effective surface slope', lists symbols including ES, and notes that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension = 1). This supports ES being dimensionless (all-zero exponents) as in the candidate.

The ledger defines Po as surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is void). The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity/void fraction, uses symbols including Po, explicitly states it is a dimensionless fraction (si_dimension = 1) and cautions to confirm geometric definition, which is consistent with the ledger's portrayal. Therefore Po is correctly dimensionless in the candidate vector.
